text:

This post asks a simple question: do the three penguin species differ in body mass?

library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(knitr)

title: R Analysis: Penguin Body Mass
text:
Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER. The data were collected by Dr. Kristen Gorman and the Palmer Station LTER program, and packaged for R by Horst, Hill and Gorman (2020). It is released under a CC0 licence.
This post asks a simple question: do the three penguin species differ in body mass?

library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(knitr)

title: R Analysis: Penguin Body Mass
text:
Cleaning the data
Some penguins are missing a body mass measurement, so drop those rows.

penguins_clean <- penguins |>
  drop_na(body_mass_g)

nrow(penguins_clean)

[1] 342

title: R Analysis: Penguin Body Mass
text:
Summary table

summary_table <- penguins_clean |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_mass_g = round(mean(body_mass_g), 1),
    sd_mass_g = round(sd(body_mass_g), 1)
  )

kable(summary_table)

Table 1 shows that Gentoo penguins have the highest mean body mass, at 5076 g.

title: R Analysis: Penguin Body Mass
text:
Figure

ggplot(penguins_clean, aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "Body mass (g)")







Figure 1: Body mass of penguins by species.

title: R Analysis: Penguin Body Mass
text:
What I found
Figure 1 agrees with the table. Gentoo penguins are clearly heavier than the other two species, while Adelie and Chinstrap penguins have similar body masses.

title: Python Analysis: Penguin Body Mass
text:
Cleaning the data
Some penguins are missing a body mass measurement, so I drop those rows, and see how many remain.

penguins = load_penguins()
penguins_clean = penguins.dropna(subset=["body_mass_g"])

len(penguins_clean)

342

title: Python Analysis: Penguin Body Mass

summary_table = (
    penguins_clean
    .groupby("species", observed=True)["body_mass_g"]

)
